claim: Codon usage biases are found in all genomes and influence protein expression levels.
source: Codon usage biases are found in all genomes and influence protein expression levels.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that draws from established scientific consensus about codon usage.

claim: The codon usage effect on protein expression was thought to be mainly due to its impact on translation.
source: The codon usage effect on protein expression was thought to be mainly due to its impact on translation.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific understanding prior to this study.

claim: Introduction of rare codons results in premature transcription termination (PTT) within open reading frames in Neurospora crassa.
source: Using Neurospora crassa as a model organism, we demonstrated that introduction of rare codons results in premature transcription termination (PTT) within open reading frames and abolishment of full-length mRNA.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Introduction of rare codons abolishes full-length mRNA in Neurospora crassa.
source: Using Neurospora crassa as a model organism, we demonstrated that introduction of rare codons results in premature transcription termination (PTT) within open reading frames and abolishment of full-length mRNA.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: PTT is a wide-spread phenomenon in Neurospora.
source: PTT is a wide-spread phenomenon in Neurospora, and there is a strong negative correlation between codon usage bias and PTT events.
evidence: This is supported by genome-wide 2P-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There is a strong negative correlation between codon usage bias and PTT events in Neurospora.
source: PTT is a wide-spread phenomenon in Neurospora, and there is a strong negative correlation between codon usage bias and PTT events.
evidence: This correlation is demonstrated through genome-wide analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Rare codons lead to the formation of putative poly(A) signals.
source: Rare codons lead to the formation of putative poly(A) signals and PTT.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that rare codons create PAS motifs.

claim: Rare codons lead to PTT.
source: Rare codons lead to the formation of putative poly(A) signals and PTT.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: A similar role for codon usage bias in PTT was observed in mouse cells.
source: A similar role for codon usage bias was also observed in mouse cells.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of mouse poly(A)-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Codon usage biases co-evolve with the transcription termination machinery to suppress premature termination of transcription.
source: Together, these results suggest that codon usage biases co-evolve with the transcription termination machinery to suppress premature termination of transcription and thus allow for optimal gene expression.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from the experimental data and comparative analyses.

claim: Most amino acids are encoded by two to six synonymous codons.
source: Due to the redundancy of triplet genetic codons, most amino acids are encoded by two to six synonymous codons.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the genetic code.

claim: Synonymous codons are not used with equal frequencies.
source: Synonymous codons are not used with equal frequencies, a phenomenon called codon usage bias (Ikemura, 1985; Sharp et al., 1986; Comeron, 2004; Plotkin and Kudla, 2011; Hershberg and Petrov, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Highly expressed proteins are mostly encoded by genes with preferred codons.
source: Highly expressed proteins are mostly encoded by genes with preferred codons, and codon optimization has been routinely used to enhance heterologous protein expression.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Codon optimization has been routinely used to enhance heterologous protein expression.
source: Highly expressed proteins are mostly encoded by genes with preferred codons, and codon optimization has been routinely used to enhance heterologous protein expression.
evidence: This is established practice in molecular biology.

claim: Positive correlations between codon usage and protein expression levels are observed in different organisms.
source: In addition, positive correlations between codon usage and protein expression levels are observed in different organisms (Hiraoka et al., 2009; Duret and Mouchiroud, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Codon usage plays an important role in regulating gene expression levels.
source: These results suggest that codon usage plays an important role in regulating gene expression levels.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited correlations and observations.

claim: Efficient and accurate translation was thought to be a major selection force for codon usage biases.
source: Efficient and accurate translation was thought to be a major selection force for codon usage biases (Hiraoka et al., 2009; Duret and Mouchiroud, 1999; Akashi, 1994; Drummond and Wilke, 2008; Xu et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2013a; Lampson et al., 2013; Pershing et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Codon usage affects co-translational protein folding by regulating translation elongation rate in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.
source: Recent studies also demonstrated that codon usage affects co-translational protein folding by regulating translation elongation rate in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes (Zhou et al., 2013a; Spencer et al., 2012; Pechmann et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2015; Fu et al., 2016; Zhao et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Overall translation efficiency is mainly determined by translation initiation.
source: Although the correlation between codon usage and gene expression level can be explained by translation efficiency, recent studies suggest that overall translation efficiency is mainly determined by translation initiation, a process that is mostly determined by RNA structure but not codon usage near the translational start site (Kudla et al., 2009; Pop et al., 2014; Tuller et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Translation initiation is mostly determined by RNA structure but not codon usage near the translational start site.
source: Although the correlation between codon usage and gene expression level can be explained by translation efficiency, recent studies suggest that overall translation efficiency is mainly determined by translation initiation, a process that is mostly determined by RNA structure but not codon usage near the translational start site (Kudla et al., 2009; Pop et al., 2014; Tuller et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Codon usage is an important determinant of RNA levels in many organisms.
source: In addition, codon usage was found to be an important determinant of RNA levels in many organisms (Presnyak et al., 2015; Boël et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2016; Kudla et al., 2006; Krinner et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In some organisms, codon usage affects RNA stability.
source: In some organisms, codon usage was shown to affect RNA stability (Presnyak et al., 2015; Boël et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2016; Kudla et al., 2006; Krinner et al., 2014; Mishima and Tomari, 2016; Bazzini et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In Neurospora and mammalian cells, codon usage is an important determinant of gene transcription levels.
source: In Neurospora and mammalian cells, codon usage has also been shown to be an important determinant of gene transcription levels (Zhou et al., 2016; Newman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Codon usage can regulate gene expression beyond the translation process.
source: Therefore, codon usage can regulate gene expression beyond the translation process.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited studies showing effects on RNA levels and transcription.

claim: In eukaryotes, the maturation of mRNA is a two-step process involving endonucleolytic cleavage of the nascent RNA followed by the synthesis of the polyadenosine (poly(A)) tail.
source: In eukaryotes, the maturation of mRNA is a two-step process involving endonucleolytic cleavage of the nascent RNA followed by the synthesis of the polyadenosine (poly(A)) tail (Tian and Graber, 2012; Shi and Manley, 2015; Proudfoot, 2011; Proudfoot, 2016; Tian and Manley, 2017; Kuehner et al., 2011; Porrua and Libri, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Polyadenylation sites are defined by surrounding cis-elements recognized by multiple proteins.
source: The polyadenylation sites, also known as the poly(A) sites or pA sites, are defined by surrounding cis-elements recognized by multiple proteins.
evidence: This is established knowledge about transcription termination.

claim: Poly(A) signals are generally AU-rich sequences and have conserved nucleotide composition in eukaryotes.
source: These cis-elements, called poly(A) signals, are generally AU-rich sequences and have conserved nucleotide composition in eukaryotes.
evidence: This is established knowledge about poly(A) signals.

claim: In mammals, the hexamer AAUAAA (or other close variants) is one of the most prominent poly(A) signals.
source: In mammals, the hexamer AAUAAA (or other close variants), referred as polyadenylation signal (PAS), is one of the most prominent poly(A) signals.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian poly(A) signals.

claim: Upstream U-rich elements, downstream U-rich element, and downstream GU-rich element play important roles in the transcription termination process in mammals.
source: Other cis-elements, such as upstream U-rich elements, downstream U-rich element, and downstream GU-rich element, also play important roles in the transcription termination process.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian transcription termination.

claim: In yeast, poly(A) signals include an upstream efficiency element (EE), an upstream position element (PE), and two U-rich elements flanking the poly(A) sites.
source: In yeast, poly(A) signals include an upstream efficiency element (EE), an upstream position element (PE), which is equivalent to PAS in mammals, and two U-rich elements flanking the poly(A) sites (Moqtaderi et al., 2013; Mata, 2013; Ozsolak et al., 2010; Schlackow et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Mutation of poly(A) signals impairs the efficiency of transcription termination and leads to defect in mRNA processing.
source: Mutation of these poly(A) signals impairs the efficiency of transcription termination and leads to defect in mRNA processing (Tian and Graber, 2012; Shi and Manley, 2015; Proudfoot, 2011; Proudfoot, 2016; Tian and Manley, 2017; Kuehner et al., 2011; Porrua and Libri, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Most transcriptional events terminate in 3' untranslated region (3' UTR) of protein-coding genes.
source: Although most of the transcriptional events terminate in 3' untranslated region (3' UTR) of protein-coding genes, premature transcription termination (PTT) also occurs in 5' UTR, intron and exon, which is also referred as premature cleavage and polyadenylation (PCPA) (Tian et al., 2007; Kaida et al., 2010; Berg et al., 2012; Jan et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2017b; Ulitsky et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Premature transcription termination (PTT) occurs in 5' UTR, intron and exon.
source: Although most of the transcriptional events terminate in 3' untranslated region (3' UTR) of protein-coding genes, premature transcription termination (PTT) also occurs in 5' UTR, intron and exon, which is also referred as premature cleavage and polyadenylation (PCPA) (Tian et al., 2007; Kaida et al., 2010; Berg et al., 2012; Jan et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2017b; Ulitsky et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Premature transcription termination occurs in the intron of the Arabidopsis FCA gene and is involved in the control of flowering timing.
source: For example, premature transcription termination occurs in the intron of the Arabidopsis FCA gene and is involved in the control of flowering timing (Quesada et al., 2003; Macknight et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: PCPA in intron is a conserved regulatory mechanism for CstF-77 gene from fly to human.
source: Moreover, PCPA in intron is a conserved regulatory mechanism for CstF-77 gene from fly to human (Mitchelson et al., 1993; Pan et al., 2006; Luo et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: PCPA within introns is a widespread phenomenon in eukaryotes.
source: Recent genome-wide studies have shown that PCPA within introns is a widespread phenomenon in eukaryotes (Tian et al., 2007; Liu et al., 2017b; van Hoof et al., 2002; Frischmeyer et al., 2002; Mayr and Bartel, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to genome-wide studies.

claim: PCPA occurs within coding regions.
source: In addition, PCPA also occurs within coding regions (Tian et al., 2007; Kaida et al., 2010; Jan et al., 2011; Dunlap and Loros, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The expression of heterologous gene can be suppressed due to PCPA in coding regions.
source: It has been shown that the expression of heterologous gene can be suppressed due to PCPA in coding regions (Diehn et al., 1998; Tokuoka et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: PCPA occurs in coding regions of endogenous genes in both yeast and human.
source: PCPA also occurs in coding regions of endogenous genes in both yeast and human (van Hoof et al., 2002; Frischmeyer et al., 2002; Georis et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Many poly(A) sites have been mapped to coding regions using poly(A) sequencing methods.
source: Importantly, many poly(A) sites have been mapped to coding regions using poly(A) sequencing methods (Jan et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2017b; Ulitsky et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to sequencing studies.

claim: Codon optimization has been previously shown to increase heterologous gene expression in Aspergillus oryzae.
source: Codon optimization has been previously shown to increase heterologous gene expression in Aspergillus oryzae (Tokuoka et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The effect of codon usage on premature transcription termination of endogenous genes is not clear.
source: However, the effect of codon usage on premature transcription termination of endogenous genes is not clear.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Neurospora crassa exhibits a strong codon usage bias for C or G at wobble positions.
source: The filamentous fungus Neurospora crassa exhibits a strong codon usage bias for C or G at wobble positions and has been an important model organism studying the roles of codon usage biases (Zhou et al., 2013a; Yu et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2015; Radford and Parish, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Neurospora crassa has been an important model organism studying the roles of codon usage biases.
source: The filamentous fungus Neurospora crassa exhibits a strong codon usage bias for C or G at wobble positions and has been an important model organism studying the roles of codon usage biases (Zhou et al., 2013a; Yu et al., 2015; Zhou et al., 2015; Radford and Parish, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In Neurospora, codon usage is a major determinant of gene expression levels and correlates strongly with protein and RNA levels.
source: In Neurospora, codon usage is a major determinant of gene expression levels and correlates strongly with protein and RNA levels (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Codon usage can regulate mRNA levels at the level of transcription by influencing chromatin structure.
source: We showed previously that codon usage can regulate mRNA levels at the level of transcription by influencing chromatin structure (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: Premature transcription termination within open reading frames is affected by codon usage bias in Neurospora.
source: In this study, we showed that premature transcription termination within open reading frames is affected by codon usage bias.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: A similar phenomenon of codon usage affecting PTT is observed in mouse.
source: Moreover, a similar phenomenon is observed in mouse, another C/G-biased organism.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of mouse data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Transcription termination serves as a conserved driving force in shaping codon usage biases in C/G-biased organisms.
source: Therefore, in addition to effects on translation, transcription termination serves as a conserved driving force in shaping codon usage biases in C/G-biased organisms.
evidence: This is the main conclusion inferred from the data presented in the study.

claim: Codon optimization of frq leads to changes in FRQ expression level and protein structure.
source: We previously showed that codon optimization of circadian clock gene frequency (frq) leads to changes in FRQ expression level and protein structure (Zhou et al., 2013a; Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research by the authors.

claim: In the frq-deopt1 construct, 59 codons were replaced by non-optimal codons.
source: In the frq-deopt1 construct, 59 codons were replaced by non-optimal codons.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental construct.

claim: In the frq-deopt2 construct, 98 codons were replaced by the least preferred codons.
source: In the frq-deopt2 construct, 98 codons were replaced by the least preferred codons (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental construct with reference to a figure.

claim: In strains expressing wild-type frq, the production of conidia was rhythmic with a period of about 22 hr.
source: In the strains expressing the wild-type frq construct, the production of conidia (asexual spore) was rhythmic with a period of about 22 hr (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The conidiation rhythm of strains expressing the two codon-deoptimized frq constructs was abolished.
source: However, the conidiation rhythm of the strains expressing the two codon-deoptimized frq constructs was abolished, indicating that the deoptimized frq genes are not functional (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The deoptimized frq genes are not functional.
source: However, the conidiation rhythm of the strains expressing the two codon-deoptimized frq constructs was abolished, indicating that the deoptimized frq genes are not functional (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of conidiation rhythm.

claim: No FRQ expression was detected in either of the deoptimized strains by western blot.
source: Surprisingly, no FRQ expression was detected in either of the deoptimized strains by western blot (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: No full-length frq mRNA was produced in the deoptimized strains.
source: Northern blot and strand-specific RT-qPCR using a set of primers targeting the middle region of frq ORF showed that no full-length frq mRNA was produced in the deoptimized strains (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1D and 1E.

claim: The introduction of rare synonymous codons within the amino-terminal region of frq abolishes the expression of full-length frq mRNA.
source: Together, these results indicate that the introduction of rare synonymous codons within this region of frq abolishes the expression of full-length frq mRNA.
evidence: This is concluded from the experimental data presented.

claim: Rare codons can result in gene silencing through histone H3 trimethylation at lysine 9 (H3K9me3).
source: We have previously shown that rare codons can result in gene silencing through histone H3 trimethylation at lysine 9 (H3K9me3), and the wild-type frq locus is marked by H3K9me3 (Zhou et al., 2016; Dang et al., 2013; Belden et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The wild-type frq locus is marked by H3K9me3.
source: We have previously shown that rare codons can result in gene silencing through histone H3 trimethylation at lysine 9 (H3K9me3), and the wild-type frq locus is marked by H3K9me3 (Zhou et al., 2016; Dang et al., 2013; Belden et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The H3K9me3 levels at the frq locus were comparable in the wild-type frq and frq-deopt2 strains.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay using an H3K9me3 antibody, however, showed that the H3K9me3 levels at the frq locus were comparable in the wild-type frq and frq-deopt2 strains (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B), suggesting that the loss of full-length frq mRNA in the deoptimized frq is not due to H3K9me3-mediated transcriptional silencing.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The loss of full-length frq mRNA in the deoptimized frq is not due to H3K9me3-mediated transcriptional silencing.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay using an H3K9me3 antibody, however, showed that the H3K9me3 levels at the frq locus were comparable in the wild-type frq and frq-deopt2 strains (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B), suggesting that the loss of full-length frq mRNA in the deoptimized frq is not due to H3K9me3-mediated transcriptional silencing.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparable H3K9me3 levels.

claim: Transcription of frq is activated by the binding of the complex of White Collar-1 (WC-1) and White Collar-2 (WC-2) to the frq promoter.
source: Transcription of frq is activated by the binding of the complex of White Collar-1 (WC-1) and White Collar-2 (WC-2) to the frq promoter, and the expression of FRQ inhibits WC binding (Heintzen and Liu, 2007; Dunlap, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The expression of FRQ inhibits WC binding.
source: Transcription of frq is activated by the binding of the complex of White Collar-1 (WC-1) and White Collar-2 (WC-2) to the frq promoter, and the expression of FRQ inhibits WC binding (Heintzen and Liu, 2007; Dunlap, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: WC-2 binding at the frq promoter was elevated in the frq-deopt2 strain.
source: A ChIP assay showed that WC-2 binding at the frq promoter was elevated in the frq-deopt2 strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the loss of full-length frq mRNA expression is not due to transcriptional gene silencing.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The loss of full-length frq mRNA expression is not due to transcriptional gene silencing.
source: A ChIP assay showed that WC-2 binding at the frq promoter was elevated in the frq-deopt2 strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the loss of full-length frq mRNA expression is not due to transcriptional gene silencing.
evidence: This is inferred from the elevated WC-2 binding.

claim: The frq pre-mRNA was increased significantly in the frq-deopt2 strain.
source: Consistent with this result, strand-specific RT-qPCR using a set of primers targeted to an intronic region in the 5' UTR of frq showed that the frq pre-mRNA was increased significantly in the frq-deopt2 strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Even though full-length frq mRNA could not be detected in the codon deoptimized strains, the transcription of frq was actually significantly increased.
source: These results indicate that even though full-length frq mRNA could not be detected in the codon deoptimized strains, the transcription of frq was actually significantly increased.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased pre-mRNA and WC-2 binding.

claim: Truncated frq mRNAs but not full-length frq mRNA were detected in both of the deoptimized frq strains.
source: As expected, truncated frq mRNAs but not full-length frq mRNA were detected in both of the deoptimized frq strains (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The truncated frq mRNA species were enriched after oligo-dT purification.
source: Like the full-length frq mRNA, the truncated frq mRNA species were also enriched after oligo-dT purification (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A cluster of 3' ends within the deoptimized region (112-141nt downstream of the start codon) of frq genes was observed.
source: We observed a cluster of 3' ends within the deoptimized region (112-141nt downstream of the start codon) of frq genes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by 3' RACE data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: PAS variants (AUAAAU in the frq-deopt1 and AUAAAA in the frq-deopt2) were created by codon deoptimization of frq.
source: Interestingly, PAS variants (AUAAAU in the frq-deopt1 and AUAAAA in the frq-deopt2), which were located in 18-nt upstream of mapped poly(A) sites, were created by codon deoptimization of frq, suggesting these truncated mRNAs may be produced by PAS-dependent pathway (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The truncated mRNAs may be produced by PAS-dependent pathway.
source: Interestingly, PAS variants (AUAAAU in the frq-deopt1 and AUAAAA in the frq-deopt2), which were located in 18-nt upstream of mapped poly(A) sites, were created by codon deoptimization of frq, suggesting these truncated mRNAs may be produced by PAS-dependent pathway (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is speculated based on the presence of PAS variants.

claim: The pol II levels at the frq promoter and 5' UTR were comparable in the wt-frq-aq and frq-deopt2-aq strains.
source: The pol II levels at the frq promoter and 5' UTR were comparable in the wt-frq-aq and frq-deopt2-aq strains, but pol II levels in the middle and 3' end of frq ORF were decreased dramatically in the frq-deopt2-aq strain compared to the wt-frq-aq strain (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Pol II levels in the middle and 3' end of frq ORF were decreased dramatically in the frq-deopt2-aq strain compared to the wt-frq-aq strain.
source: The pol II levels at the frq promoter and 5' UTR were comparable in the wt-frq-aq and frq-deopt2-aq strains, but pol II levels in the middle and 3' end of frq ORF were decreased dramatically in the frq-deopt2-aq strain compared to the wt-frq-aq strain (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Codon deoptimization of frq abolished its expression due to premature transcription termination.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that codon deoptimization of frq abolished its expression due to premature transcription termination.
evidence: This is concluded from the ChIP and other experimental data.

claim: Codon deoptimization of frq resulted in the premature transcription termination of qrf.
source: Codon deoptimization of frq also resulted in the premature transcription termination of qrf as indicated by the loss of full-length qrf and appearance of truncated qrf mRNA in the frq-deopt1 and frq-deopt2 strains (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The 3' ends of the truncated qrf mRNAs in the frq-deopt1 strains localized in the deoptimized region with a potential PAS (AUAAAA) motif 21-nt upstream of the 3' ends.
source: 3' RACE result showed that the 3' ends of the truncated qrf mRNAs in the frq-deopt1 strains also localized in the deoptimized region with a potential PAS (AUAAAA) motif 21-nt upstream of the 3' ends (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by 3' RACE data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The wt-frq gene has the same putative PAS motif as the deoptimized constructs.
source: It should be noted that the wt-frq gene also has the same putative PAS motif, suggesting that the nucleotide sequence near PAS motif is also required for transcription termination.
evidence: This is observed from sequence analysis.

claim: The nucleotide sequence near PAS motif is also required for transcription termination.
source: It should be noted that the wt-frq gene also has the same putative PAS motif, suggesting that the nucleotide sequence near PAS motif is also required for transcription termination.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that wt-frq has the same PAS motif but does not undergo PTT.

claim: Neither full-length frq mRNA nor FRQ protein was detected in the frq-deopt3 strain.
source: Neither full-length frq mRNA nor FRQ protein was detected in the frq-deopt3 strain (Figure 3B and C), suggesting that the deoptimized region in frq-deopt3 contains all elements sufficient to trigger transcription termination.
evidence: This is supported by northern and western blot data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: The deoptimized region in frq-deopt3 contains all elements sufficient to trigger transcription termination.
source: Neither full-length frq mRNA nor FRQ protein was detected in the frq-deopt3 strain (Figure 3B and C), suggesting that the deoptimized region in frq-deopt3 contains all elements sufficient to trigger transcription termination.
evidence: This is inferred from the complete loss of full-length mRNA and protein.

claim: The prematurely terminated products in the frq-deopt3 strain may be rapidly degraded by the RNA quality control mechanisms.
source: The low level of the prematurely terminated products in the frq-deopt3 strain, suggesting that these products may be rapidly degraded by the RNA quality control mechanisms (van Hoof et al., 2002; Frischmeyer et al., 2002; Doma and Parker, 2007; Vanacova and Stefl, 2007; Schmid and Jensen, 2010).
evidence: This is speculated based on the low levels of terminated products and supported by citations.

claim: Both full-length frq RNA and FRQ protein were detected in the frq-deopt4 strain, but their levels were significantly lower than that in the wt-frq strain.
source: In the frq-deopt4 strain, both full-length frq RNA and FRQ protein were detected, but their levels were significantly lower than that in the wt-frq strain (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is supported by northern and western blot data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: PolII levels at the frq transcription start site were comparable in the wt-frq and frq-deopt4 strains.
source: ChIP result showed that polII levels at the frq transcription start site were comparable in the wt-frq and frq-deopt4 strains (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the decrease of full-length frq mRNA in the frq-deopt4 strain was not due to transcriptional silencing.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The decrease of full-length frq mRNA in the frq-deopt4 strain was not due to transcriptional silencing.
source: ChIP result showed that polII levels at the frq transcription start site were comparable in the wt-frq and frq-deopt4 strains (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the decrease of full-length frq mRNA in the frq-deopt4 strain was not due to transcriptional silencing.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparable polII levels.

claim: The level of premature terminated frq RNAs in the frq-deopt4 strain was lower than that in the frq-deopt2 strain.
source: Notably, the level of premature terminated frq RNAs in the frq-deopt4 strain was also lower than that in the frq-deopt2 strain, suggesting that transcription termination efficiency was decreased due to the lack of some elements.
evidence: This is observed from the experimental data.

claim: Transcription termination efficiency was decreased in frq-deopt4 due to the lack of some elements.
source: Notably, the level of premature terminated frq RNAs in the frq-deopt4 strain was also lower than that in the frq-deopt2 strain, suggesting that transcription termination efficiency was decreased due to the lack of some elements.
evidence: This is inferred from the lower levels of terminated products.

claim: The levels of frq mRNA and FRQ protein in the frq-deopt5 strain were higher than those in the frq-deopt4 strain but were much lower than those in the wt-frq strain.
